summary: The split is sound and the compatibility gate is the load-bearing half. Two findings are about the change itself. Four are about the skill mode that produced it: running /cobuilder-architect:design against this design surfaced that architecture's design mode writes an ADR and nothing else, so every design-directory artifact the viewer renders had to be written by hand afterwards.

findings.title: Architecture design mode does not know design directories exist
findings.detail: skills/architecture/SKILL.md's Design Mode section names one output: an ADR markdown document, optionally with an HTML version. The design directory — goal.json, intent.json, narrative.json, assessment.json, diagrams/ — came from the odyssey design mode and is specified in skills/odyssey/references/design-mode.md. Session decision 3 folds odyssey design into the architect pillar, but the architecture skill was never given that responsibility. Running the mode therefore produced two well-formed ADRs and no design at all. The Designs view stayed empty because nothing in the mode it ran was ever told to fill it.
findings.mitigation: Design mode's Output section must name the design directory as a first-class output alongside the ADR, and reference the seven stages in design-mode.md rather than stopping at the corpus chain. This is merge debt from folding the two skills together, not a new feature.

findings.title: narrative.json is the only design artifact with no projection and no validation
findings.detail: build_designs.py projects goal, intent, and assessment through explicit field tuples (GOAL_FIELDS, INTENT_FIELDS, ASSESSMENT_FIELDS) and validates their shape. narrative.json is attached raw at line 277 with one isinstance check. Its four-level structure — landscape, problem_solution, architecture, file_changes — is written down nowhere: not in the script, not in the architecture skill, not in a template. An author has to read design-mode/narrative.json and infer the shape. A missing or misshapen level fails silently in the viewer rather than loudly in the build.
findings.mitigation: Give narrative.json a NARRATIVE_FIELDS projection and a per-level check, the same treatment the other three artifacts already get. Add the level shape to the design-mode reference so it can be authored without reverse-engineering an example.

findings.title: verify_bundle checks PRs level by level and designs file-by-existence
findings.detail: check_designs() returns ok when data/designs.js parses as an object assignment. It never looks inside a design. A design carrying only goal.json passes as ok, which is exactly what happened here. The per-PR checks verify each of the four narrative levels, each asset, and each diagram individually. Two artifact families feed the same four-level viewer under two completely different standards of proof.
findings.mitigation: Extend check_designs to report per-design completeness in the same vocabulary the PR checks use, with narrative levels required and intent, assessment, and diagrams optional.

findings.title: The corpus path in the skill body does not match the corpus on disk
findings.detail: SKILL.md and corpus-index.md both reference corpus/principles/... The files live at references/corpus/principles/... A first read from the skill base directory finds nothing.
findings.mitigation: Make the paths relative to the skill base directory, or state the base the paths are relative to.

findings.title: The compatibility gate is only as good as its least-updated vendored copy
findings.detail: require_compatible() lives in a module each plugin vendors. A plugin forked before the function existed carries no gate, and the safety property collapses without a signal. The one-tag release discipline narrows this to cross-tag skew but does not close it, because nothing in the install mechanism enforces a shared tag.
findings.mitigation: Have the writer record its own key in the generators map on every write. A bundle whose generators map holds a plugin that never advanced its key is then visible evidence of an ungated writer, rather than an invisible one.

findings.title: Neither ADR can reach approved, because the context they map to does not exist
findings.detail: ADR-0016 and ADR-0017 both anchor maps_to at context cobuilder-packaging. docs/architecture/contexts/ is empty, so there is no boundary.yaml carrying the invariant either record establishes. The decision-records standard requires that anchor.
findings.mitigation: Run /cobuilder-architect:describe for cobuilder-packaging before either record leaves tentative. That is epic E5.

boundary_checks.rule: No agents, no hooks, no MCP servers in the install surface
boundary_checks.note: The split adds manifests and symlinks only.

boundary_checks.rule: Authored source lives in docs/, derived projections in the bundle
boundary_checks.note: shared/ is authored source at the marketplace root, outside both.

boundary_checks.rule: Architecture modes are self-only and refuse a foreign target
boundary_checks.note: The split does not move any mode across that line.

drift.title: Two design modes still coexist
drift.detail: skills/odyssey/references/design-mode.md and skills/architecture/SKILL.md both define a design mode. Decision 3 folds one into the other. Until that lands, which mode a user gets depends on which command they type, and only one of them writes a design directory.
